item.title: Repeated near misses at junction, 8th October
item.description:
I am writing to raise a serious road safety concern regarding the junction at by the Co-Op on the Homelands estate in Bishops Cleeve. I regularly travel through this junction along the priority road, continuing straight ahead. Unfortunately, I have experienced multiple near misses with vehicles approaching from the adjoining roads, failing to give way and driving straight across the junction at speed. On several occasions, I have come dangerously close to being involved in a side-impact collision because other drivers have failed to recognise or observe the giveway markings. This is not an isolated incident. It happens frequently enough that I now find myself bracing for a potential collision every time I approach the junction, despite having priority. I appreciate that individual driver behaviour cannot always be controlled. However, the frequency of these incidents makes me question whether the junction layout, road markings or signage are sufficiently clear to approaching motorists. To be brutally honest, I think it’s only a matter of time until somebody is seriously injured or killed here. I would like to request that the council considers conducting a road safety assessment of this junction, particularly looking at: - The visibility and clarity of the existing give\-way markings and signage. - Whether the layout makes it sufficiently obvious which road has priority. - Whether additional warning signs, improved road markings or traffic-calming measures could reduce the risk of collisions. I have attached a photograph of the junction, with an arrow indicating my usual direction of travel, to help illustrate my concern. My husband also drives this route and had a near miss today which is why I’m sending this - I have also had a near miss this week. I would appreciate confirmation that this concern has been recorded and information about whether the junction can be assessed for potential safety improvements. Thank you

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Unit 1, Vale Road, Bishop's Cleeve, Cheltenham

item.title: Leylandii trees obscuring light making it difficult to see walking down alleyway, 8th October
item.description:
Good afternoon, It has been reported to me that there is an issue with the footpath that leads between Boverton Drive and Boverton Avenue. Apparently there are Leylandii trees in the garden of number 34 Boverton Avenue that are very overgrown and over hanging the alleyway making the street light ineffective. This is a well used alleyway and if pedestrians cannot see at night it could have health and safety implications. There is also apparently an issue with dog mess not being picked up (despite the fact there is a dog poo bin at the end of the alleyway) it may be that not being able to see properly at night in order to pick up their dogs mess may be contributing to this problem. It has been reported to TBC who have said that they do not own the land that is the alleyway between Boverton Drive and Boverton Avenue so I am assuming this is a highways issue. Perhaps you could contact the owner of number 34 and request they cut back their Leylandii to help with lighting in the alleyway. Many thanks Lianne Eve Clerk to Brockworth Parish Council

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 31, Boverton Avenue, Coopers Edge, Gloucester
Report on FixMyStreet
